summary: Nanjing suits layered city travel that combines Republican-era streets, major history sites, lakeside calm, and manageable old-city food routes.
transport_notes: Keep the old city, Qinhuai River, and museum-heavy areas grouped rather than crossing back and forth through the day.
Metro plus short taxi or walking connections works well for central Nanjing.
Evening plans are strongest around Qinhuai River or older walkable food districts.

budget_notes.low: Focus on city walls, public parks, old-street walks, and affordable neighborhood food.
budget_notes.medium: Combine one major heritage stop, one scenic district, and one recognizable local dining area each day.
budget_notes.high: Use a slower pace with stronger dining moments and more comfort between large historic sites.

trip_type_notes.student: Student trips in Nanjing should mix iconic history, walkable streets, and affordable local food.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should emphasize reflective history, city-wall wandering, and everyday neighborhood texture.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should soften the historical tone with riverside lights, lake views, and atmospheric old streets.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should keep landmark movement simple and leave room for rest between major heritage stops.

pois.name: Presidential Palace Area

pois.name: Laomendong
